evidence_items.locator: Production reliability and engineering challenges; paragraph beginning Debugging benefits from new approaches
evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic describes unpredictable execution and cascading behavioral changes that complicated debugging its deployed research system, but also reports successful diagnosis and repair after adding tracing. This bears directly on the forecast without establishing exceptional repair effort or routine ease.

The study reports 53.5% accuracy for identifying the responsible agent and 14.2% for identifying the failure step in its best method. This supports difficulty in automated diagnosis, but does not measure engineers' repair time or establish the forecast's degree of difficulty.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract; version 3, with submission history below
evidence_items.explanation: DoVer reports recovery of 18–28% of failed trials on GAIA and AssistantBench and 49% on GSMPlus through tested interventions. These successes qualify a pessimistic reading, but recovery of selected executions does not demonstrate inexpensive, durable fixes to deployed systems.

receipt.public_excerpt: repair effectiveness depends more on precise execution control

evidence_items.explanation: Across three frameworks and 536 failed executions, the study reports at most 6.90% repair through task-level regeneration versus 20.15% through a targeted intervention. This supports substantial reproduction and repair challenges while demonstrating progress; its benchmark experiments do not establish production debugging effort.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not establish representative engineering time or effort needed to diagnose and durably repair deployed research agents.
Automated attribution accuracy and recovery of individual executions do not establish whether system-level fixes prevent recurrence.
No agreed threshold distinguishes difficult debugging from the forecast's massively difficult debugging.
The evidence does not provide a comparable baseline for debugging effort in other complex software.
